title: eSIM Explained: How Digital SIMs Work and Who Uses Them
description: What an eSIM is, which phones support it, how to switch networks or add a travel eSIM, and the pros and cons compared with a physical SIM card.
intro: An eSIM is a SIM built into your phone and downloaded over the air. It makes switching networks and adding travel data quicker, and some newer phones no longer have a physical SIM slot.

image.alt: SIM cards and SIM adaptors laid out on a table

sections.html: Instead of inserting a plastic card, you scan a QR code or use your network’s app to download a profile to your phone. Most eSIM phones can store several profiles and use one or two at a time.

Recent iPhones, Google Pixels, Samsung Galaxy phones and many other models support eSIM, as do some smartwatches and tablets. Some US iPhone models are eSIM-only. Check your phone’s settings or the manufacturer’s site.

• Pros: instant activation, easy dual-SIM, no waiting for post, handy travel eSIMs.
  • Cons: moving to a new phone means transferring or re-downloading the profile; not every provider supports eSIM on every plan.
Your number-keeping rights are the same. In the UK, text PAC to 65075 and give the code to your new provider. In the US, ask the new carrier to port your number.
